data.narrative:
Pacific Fusion, a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Eric Lander and Will Regan, is valued within a comp universe of 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private-stage companies including Helion, X-Energy, Valar Atomics, Fuse Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy. The company has raised $900M to date.

Two valuation methods prove applicable. Stage-progression analysis uses the $900M total raised as a proxy base and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding $1.8B. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables (Valar Atomics at $6.0B in Series B, Nano Nuclear Energy at $808M in Seed, and Fuse Energy at $200M in Series A) produces a median valuation of $808M, with a range spanning $200M to $6.0B. These methods reflect the wide dispersion inherent in early-stage nuclear technology valuations.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $687M (low) to $2.1B (high), with a median of $1.3B. The gap between peer-median and stage-progression results reflects tension between current funding history and anticipated next-stage growth. Key uncertainties include technology readiness, regulatory pathway clarity, and capital intensity of commercialization—factors not directly quantified in comparable transactions.
